text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is often called the "silent killer" because it rarely causes any noticeable warning signs. Most people can live with high blood pressure for years without feeling a single clue.
snippet_highlighted_words: rarely causes any noticeable warning signs

text_blocks.snippet: Symptoms generally only show up if your blood pressure rises to dangerously high levels (a hypertensive crisis, usually above 180/120 mm Hg). At this stage, possible signs include:

list.snippet: Confusion, weakness, or trouble speaking (which can signal a stroke)
Unexplained nosebleeds or blood spots in the eyes

text_blocks.snippet: What to Do If Readings Are Very High
According to the American Heart Association:

list.snippet: Above 180/120 mm Hg without symptoms: Wait one minute and retest. If it stays that high, contact your doctor right away.
Above 180/120 mm Hg with symptoms (such as chest pain, shortness of breath, numbness, weakness, or vision changes): Call 911 immediately.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about daily tracking from the Mayo Clinic High Blood Pressure Guide.
